ptileset.title: Dynamic Tileset
ptileset.desc: After building three different tileset systems at Tequila Works, I created my own: a blueprint (based on the SuperGrid Starter Pack material) that modifies the appearance and size of a single cube usable as floor, wall, railing or interactive. Metrics live in the tileset itself, so anyone working with layouts learns them in-game without reading a document, and objects snap to fixed sizes, protecting performance from rescaled meshes.
ptileset.about:
During my years at Tequila Works I built three different tileset systems, one per project, improving the idea with every iteration. Browsing the Unreal Marketplace I found the SuperGridStarter Pack: a pack I loved, but everything in it came as separate materials, so you ended up juggling many of them. I adapted one of those materials to the system I had in mind.

The result is a single Blueprint cube whose look and size you change from the Details panel: floor, wall, railing, interactive prop, whatever the blockout needs. For performance, every material parameter is locked by default. Unreal renders a non-editable instance far more cheaply, so you only unlock what you really need.

With the metrics baked into the tileset, anyone working on layouts learns them in-game, without reading a document.
resp: Grid drawn on the object: size, opacity, colours and background texture
Normal map on/off, swappable normal texture and roughness, from smooth to marked
Pulses with their own colour, brightness and speed, so small interactive props catch the eye
Layer texture that shows an object or character with the base metrics: scale, tile, offset and flip it
A different colour per face, so one object can mean different things by colour code
Fixed scale steps (Manual Scale off): metrics cannot drift by accident between blockout and environment
Rescaled meshes raise draw calls, so the actor only scales to approved sizes

pfinder.title: BP_ActorFinder
pfinder.meta: Personal · Unreal Engine 4 · Blueprint tool · born on Rime
pfinder.desc: On Rime we had serious performance problems on an engine we didn’t fully control. BP_ActorFinder scans the level and flags problem actors, making it much easier to find mistakes accumulated during map development.
pfinder.about:
On Rime we had serious performance problems and little idea of what was going on: we had paid to move to an engine we did not fully control. Objects were disappearing, there were more draw calls than usual, too many unknowns. So I built BP_ActorFinder, a Blueprint that helped us learn as we went along.

It made it much easier to catch the mistakes we were making while developing the maps and to know which object had which problem. It helped find and fix many small issues that had piled up over time.
resp: Objects sitting at 0,0,0
Objects with more than X materials
Rescaled objects
Objects not visible in game
Objects with the mesh set to null
Tick enabled, or disabled, by default
Any other check we needed as the project went on

pdebug.meta: Personal · Unreal Engine 4 · Blueprint tool · WIP
pdebug.desc: A blueprint placed on the stage that opens a side panel with multiple options to speed up development: cheats for testing, viewport manipulation to find visual problems, filtering by objects added to levels, gameplay tweaks and engine values in the Debug tab.
pdebug.about:
BP_DebugMenu is a Blueprint you drop into the level: with a configurable button combination it opens a side panel with multiple options meant to make the project easier to develop.

It is unfinished and several functions do not work properly yet, but the idea stands: everything that helps a developer do the job faster and with less friction, in one place.
resp: Cheats that help test things quickly
Viewport manipulation to find visual problems
Filters by the objects added to each level
In-game gameplay modifiers
Engine values editable from the Debug tab
